scope: Read-only reconciliation of current 28 readings, 34 article figures, book placement metadata and supplied live HTML audit
independent_checks: Recomputed all 34 original source SHA256 values; all match evidence and are distinct
Recomputed all 34 published delivery JPEG hashes; all are distinct
Both book placement inventories contain 34 distinct original hashes
Local hub HTML contains the overview image twice; live report independently records the same banner and overview-card reuse
Live report includes 29 HTTP-200 routes and matching figures for all article routes; this reviewer reconciled the report but did not independently refetch remote pages
conclusions: No same-original or same-delivery-image duplication across the 34 active article figure placements
Related-reading previews intentionally reuse destination illustrations or portraits; responsive image sizes are not additional originals
Old maya-miriga-documentary and bhukha-documentary filename prefixes belong to Nirad and Sabyasachi portraits respectively, not duplicate current film illustrations
Different desk compositions may feel visually similar, but exact/hash evidence does not identify them as reused art

presentation_observation.recommendation: Describe this literal within-page repeat honestly; if reducing repetition is desired, use a text-led featured introduction or a different existing banner, without implying duplicate article art.

limits: No blanket no-repetition claim across the entire website: site logos, related cards, hub banner/card and author portrait on book cover intentionally recur
Perceptual hashes are heuristic and do not prove all edited/cropped imagery unique
Book finding covers chapter/companion placement metadata, not a fresh full-PDF image extraction or pixel audit
No source edits or publication performed
